kind.ssh_invalid_user.label: SSH: unknown user
kind.ssh_preauth_fail.label: SSH: dropped before login (brute force)
kind.ssh_probe.label: SSH: port scan
kind.ssh_accepted.label: SSH: successful login
kind.web_scan.label: Web: probing for vulnerable files
kind.web_exploit.label: Web: exploit attempt
kind.web_scanner.label: Web: vulnerability scanner
kind.web_probe.label: Web: junk request / probing
kind.web_auth_fail.label: Web: access denied (401/403)
kind.web_sensitive_served.label: Web: sensitive file SERVED
kind.f2b_ban.label: fail2ban: IP banned
kind.supabase_auth_fail.label: Supabase Auth: failed login
kind.supabase_rate_limit.label: Supabase: rate limit exceeded
kind.ssh_failed_password.explain: Someone is guessing an SSH password or key. Dangerous only if password login is enabled and the password is weak.
kind.ssh_invalid_user.explain: Guessing user names such as admin, test or oracle. Normal internet background: bots try common names.
kind.ssh_preauth_fail.explain: The connection closed before login. With key-only login, almost all brute force looks like this: bots try and leave.
kind.ssh_probe.explain: A scanner checks which service is on the port and never gets to the login.
kind.web_scan.explain: Looking for well-known files and panels (.env, .git, wp-admin, phpMyAdmin). Dangerous only if the file is actually served.
kind.web_exploit.explain: The URL shows signs of an attack: path traversal, SQL injection, Log4Shell, command injection.
kind.web_scanner.explain: User-Agent of a known scanner (sqlmap, nikto, nuclei, masscan and others).
kind.web_probe.explain: Malformed request: TLS on an HTTP port, binary junk, an empty request. Bots use these to find out what is listening on the port.
kind.web_sensitive_served.explain: The server answered 2xx to a request for a secret file (.env, .git, a database dump). This may be a leak: check it now.
kind.f2b_ban.explain: fail2ban banned the IP after a series of failed attempts.
kind.supabase_auth_fail.explain: Failed login through Supabase Auth (wrong password, invalid token).
kind.supabase_rate_limit.explain: Supabase rejected requests over the rate limit: possible brute force or flooding.
finding.sshd_config_missing.title: SSH configuration not found
finding.sshd_config_missing.detail: /etc/ssh/sshd_config is not mounted into the container, so the SSH check was skipped.
finding.ssh_empty_passwords.title: SSH allows empty passwords
finding.ssh_empty_passwords.detail: PermitEmptyPasswords yes: accounts with an empty password can log in without one.
finding.ssh_empty_passwords.fix: Set PermitEmptyPasswords no and reload sshd.
finding.ssh_password_auth.title: SSH allows password login
finding.ssh_password_auth.detail: PasswordAuthentication = yes (explicitly or by default). Password brute force can eventually succeed.
finding.ssh_password_auth.fix:
First make sure key login works, and keep the current session open. Then:
echo 'PasswordAuthentication no' | sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-hardening.conf
echo 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication no' | sudo tee -a /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-hardening.conf
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
A file with the 00- prefix is read before 50-cloud-init.conf, and in sshd the first value wins.
finding.ssh_root_password.title: Root can log in with a password
finding.ssh_root_password.fix: Set PermitRootLogin prohibit-password (key only), or no if there is a separate user with sudo.
finding.ssh_root_key.title: Root logs in with a key
finding.ssh_root_key.detail: PermitRootLogin prohibit-password: the root password cannot be guessed, login is by key only.
finding.ssh_root_key.fix: Acceptable. Stricter: a separate user with sudo and PermitRootLogin no.
finding.ssh_maxauthtries.title: MaxAuthTries = {value}
finding.ssh_maxauthtries.detail: Many attempts per connection make brute force easier.
finding.ssh_x11.title: X11Forwarding is enabled
finding.ssh_x11.detail: An unneeded feature on a server without a GUI.
finding.no_fail2ban.title: fail2ban not found
finding.no_fail2ban.detail: No /etc/fail2ban: IPs that brute-force SSH are not banned automatically (or the directory is not mounted into the container).
finding.no_fail2ban.fix:
sudo apt install fail2ban (the sshd jail is enabled by default).
Check: sudo fail2ban-client status sshd
finding.ufw_disabled.title: ufw firewall is disabled
finding.ufw_disabled.detail: ENABLED=no in /etc/ufw/ufw.conf. If you use Hetzner Cloud Firewall, check that it blocks everything except 22/80/443.
finding.ufw_disabled.fix: sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw allow 22/tcp && sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp && sudo ufw enable
finding.unreadable.title: Cannot read log {path}
finding.unreadable.detail: The monitor cannot read this file, so attacks logged there are not counted.
finding.unreadable.fix: Give the monitor's user read access (the adm group or the group that owns the log).
supabase.token_rejected.title: Supabase: token rejected ({what} cannot be read)
supabase.token_rejected.detail: The Supabase personal access token has expired, was revoked or has no access to the project.
supabase.token_rejected.fix: Create a new token (Account → Access Tokens) and replace SECWATCH_SUPABASE_TOKEN.
supabase.unavailable.title: Supabase: {what} unavailable
supabase.unavailable.detail: The Management API request failed ({error}). Supabase may have changed the API.
supabase.unavailable.fix: Check the secwatch service log and update the monitor.
rec.ssh_bruteforce_success.title: Password login from an IP that was guessing passwords the same day: {ip}
rec.ssh_bruteforce_success.detail: User {user}, {time}. This looks like a successful password guess.
rec.ssh_bruteforce_success.fix: Right now: check `last`, `who`, `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`, crontab and new processes; change the user's password; disable password login. If in doubt, treat the server as compromised.
rec.ssh_new_ip.title: Successful SSH login from a new IP {ip} ({country})
rec.ssh_new_ip.fix: Make sure it was you or someone on your team. If not, rotate the keys and check authorized_keys.
rec.sensitive.title: The server served a sensitive file: {target}
rec.sensitive.fix: Block the path in nginx right away (location ~ /\.(env|git) {{ deny all; }}), remove the file from the web root and rotate every secret it contained.
rec.f2b_silent.title: SSH brute force is going on, but fail2ban bans nobody
rec.f2b_silent.detail: {count} attempts in a day and 0 bans.
rec.f2b_silent.fix: Check: sudo fail2ban-client status sshd. On Ubuntu 24.04 the jail reads journald: set backend = systemd under [sshd] in /etc/fail2ban/jail.local.
rec.heavy_ips.title: {count} IPs with especially frequent attempts
rec.heavy_ips.fix: fail2ban is usually enough. Manually: sudo ufw deny from <IP>. Useful everywhere: CrowdSec (a shared blocklist of malicious IPs).
rec.web_exploits.title: Bots are trying web exploits
rec.web_exploits.fix: Background noise as long as the responses are 4xx. Keep Next.js, nginx and dependencies up to date, and check that none of these requests got a 200.
alert.new_login: 🔑 SSH login from a new IP {user} ← {ip} ({country}, {asn}) {detail} If this was not you, check the server now.
digest.title: 🛡 Security summary for {day}
ui.title: 🛡 secwatch: attack monitor
ui.risk_note: Hundreds of attempts a day are normal background noise for any public server. The numbers are not the danger: successful logins, leaked secrets and weak settings are. Those are listed below under "What to fix".

ui.hours.title: Attacks by hour
ui.trend.title: Last 7 days
ui.ips.title: Where attacks come from
ui.ips.no_geo: Country and network are not resolved yet. The DB-IP databases download automatically at startup (the server needs internet access), or put GeoLite2-Country.mmdb and GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb in the data directory (see README).

finding.probe_port.title: Port {port} ({service}) is open to the internet on {host}
finding.probe_port.detail: Anyone can connect to {host}:{port}. Services like this are scanned and attacked within minutes of going online.
finding.probe_port.fix: Close it in the firewall (e.g. `sudo ufw deny {port}`) or bind the service to 127.0.0.1 / a private network. If it must be public, allow only your IPs.
finding.probe_tls_invalid.title: HTTPS certificate of {host} is not valid
finding.probe_tls_invalid.detail: Browsers show a warning and connections can be intercepted: {error}.
finding.probe_tls_invalid.fix: Renew or fix the certificate (Caddy and certbot do it automatically when port 80 is reachable and DNS points to the server).
finding.probe_tls_expiring.title: HTTPS certificate of {host} expires in {days} days
finding.probe_tls_expiring.detail: Automatic renewal seems to fail; after expiry the site stops opening.
finding.probe_tls_expiring.fix: Check the renewal logs (Caddy: journalctl -u caddy; certbot: sudo certbot renew --dry-run).
finding.probe_no_https_redirect.title: {host}: plain HTTP is not redirected to HTTPS
finding.probe_no_https_redirect.detail: Visitors who type the address without https:// stay on an unencrypted connection.
finding.probe_no_https_redirect.fix: Redirect port 80 to HTTPS (Caddy does it by default; nginx: return 301 https://$host$request_uri;).
finding.probe_no_hsts.title: {host}: no HSTS header
finding.probe_no_hsts.detail: Browsers are not told to always use HTTPS for this site.
finding.probe_no_hsts.fix: Add the header Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains.
finding.probe_unreachable.title: {url} does not answer
finding.probe_unreachable.detail: The site could not be reached from the outside during the check.
finding.probe_unreachable.fix: Check that the server and the web server are running and DNS points to the right address.
finding.probe_secret_file.title: Secret file is served to anyone: {url}
finding.probe_secret_file.detail: The content looks like a real {what}. Bots look for these files every day.
finding.probe_secret_file.fix: Block the path in the web server right now, remove the file from the web root and rotate every password and key it contained.
finding.probe_api_open.title: API answers without login: {url}
finding.probe_api_open.detail: A request without any login got HTTP {status} with {size} bytes of data instead of 401/403.
finding.probe_api_open.fix: Check that this route verifies the session or API key before reading data (and that database rules, e.g. Supabase RLS, do not allow anonymous reads).
probe.report.title: secwatch external check: {targets}
probe.report.ok: Nothing exposed: no risky open ports, certificate fine, no secret files, protected APIs refuse anonymous requests.
kind.sys_boot.label: System: server started
kind.sys_boot.explain: The kernel booted: a reboot, planned (updates) or not (crash, power).
kind.sys_oom.label: System: out of memory
kind.sys_oom.explain: The kernel killed a process because memory ran out.
kind.sys_disk_error.label: System: disk error
kind.sys_disk_error.explain: Read/write errors or a file system switched to read-only: data loss risk.
kind.sys_service_failed.label: System: service failed
kind.sys_service_failed.explain: A systemd service stopped with an error.
kind.sys_user_change.label: System: users or groups changed
kind.sys_user_change.explain: A user was created or deleted, a password changed or someone was added to a group. Attackers do this to keep access.
rec.sys_user_change.title: Users or groups changed: {target} ({detail}), {time}
rec.sys_user_change.detail: New accounts, password changes and additions to sudo/docker groups are a classic way to keep access to a hacked server.
rec.sys_user_change.fix: If it was not you or your team: check `last`, `getent group sudo docker`, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of every user, and treat the server as compromised.
rec.sys_disk_error.title: Disk errors: {n} today
rec.sys_disk_error.detail: The kernel reported read/write errors or remounted a file system read-only.
rec.sys_disk_error.fix: Check `dmesg -T | grep -i error`, free space and the disk health; make sure backups are fresh.
rec.sys_oom.title: Out of memory: {n} processes killed ({targets})
rec.sys_oom.detail: When memory runs out the kernel kills processes; services restart or stop working.
rec.sys_oom.fix: Check memory use (`free -m`, `ps aux --sort=-rss | head`), add swap or memory, or limit the hungry service.
rec.sys_service_failed.title: Service failed: {unit} ({n}×)
rec.sys_service_failed.detail: The service stopped with an error today.
rec.sys_boot.title: The server started {n}× today (last at {time})
rec.sys_boot.detail: A reboot. Fine after updates; if nobody planned it, find out why.
rec.sys_boot.fix: `last -x reboot` shows reboots; `journalctl -b -1 -e` shows the end of the previous boot.
rec.new_log_events.title: New kinds of system log events: {n}
rec.new_log_events.detail: Messages this server has not produced before (a new service, an unusual error, a changed setting). Most are harmless, but this is where changes show up.
rec.new_log_events.fix: Look through the list in the System section of the dashboard.
finding.allowlist_invalid.title: Allowlist has entries that are not IPs or networks
finding.allowlist_invalid.fix: Write one IP or network per line, e.g. `203.0.113.5 office` or `198.51.100.0/24 VPN`.
digest.system: System: notable events {events}, new kinds of log events {new}
ui.logins.allowlist: Allowlist: {n} entries — their events are not counted as attacks.
ui.system.title: System: notable and new events
ui.system.none: No reboots, out-of-memory kills, disk errors, failed services or user changes today.
ui.system.new_hint: Messages never seen on this server before (learned during the first days). Values like IPs and numbers are masked.
ui.system.new_none: Nothing new today (or the monitor is still learning what is normal here).
ui.claude.hint_api: Sends today's summary (counters, attacker IPs, findings; never your own IPs or tokens) to Claude and shows a plain-language review. One answer per day is cached.
ui.claude.hint_prompt: Free: copies today's summary with instructions; paste it into Claude Code, claude.ai or another assistant. Add SECWATCH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to get the review right here.
ui.claude.copied: Copied — paste it into your assistant.
ui.claude.working: Claude is reading today's data… (up to a minute)
ui.claude.failed: Something went wrong. The prompt below can be pasted into Claude manually.
claude.error.permission: This API key has no access to the model.
claude.error.rate_limit: Claude API rate limit — try again in a minute.
claude.error.api: Claude API returned an error — try again later.
claude.error.network: Claude API is not reachable from the server.
claude.error.refusal: Claude declined to answer this request.
claude.error.empty: Claude returned an empty answer — try again.
